p01.why: The specialization and the instantiation pick which(T*), the more specialized template, and the int* call uses the specialization.

p02.why: An invented pack cannot fill a non-pack parameter, so the template with a leading T is more specialized.

p03.why: The member gets an rvalue object parameter on Clang 22 and GCC, so the call is ambiguous; Clang 18 and EDG give it an lvalue reference and pick the member.

p04.why: The two templates differ only in an ellipsis; Clang and EDG let the constraint decide, GCC finds the call ambiguous.

p05.why: For an address, the whole function types take part, so T* make and f(T*) are more specialized.

p06.why: T* is more specialized than T, and const T* than T*.

p07.why: With no target type, the constraints do not decide between functions with different parameter lists, so two functions remain.

p08.why: For one argument, the template with no pack at that position wins; for two, only the variadic one is viable.

p09.why: Only result types take part, and the lvalue reference or more qualified result wins in each class, so no static_assert body is instantiated.

p10.why: After stripping references both parameters are T, and only one was a reference, so neither is more specialized.

p11.why: A defaulted parameter counts at the pack position; GCC and EDG choose the first template, Clang finds the call ambiguous.

p12.why: The template heads differ in length; EDG lets the constraint decide, Clang and GCC find the call ambiguous.

p13.why: For results T& and const T&&, Clang finds no order; GCC and EDG choose T&.

p14.why: Clang and EDG reverse the swapped candidate and pick it as more specialized (true); GCC picks the written candidate and the assertion fails.

p15.why: The placeholder's invented parameter makes the heads equivalent, and Strong subsumes Weak.

p16.why: Inside the pair, the lvalue reference wins before the pack tie-breaker applies.

p17.why: Both bind const int&, and the more qualified reference wins.

p18.why: The result types and heads match, so the constrained conversion wins.

p19.why: The partial specializations order as function templates over their patterns.

p20.why: One pair prefers T& and the other prefers U*, so neither template is more specialized.

p21.why: The result types differ (T* and T* const); EDG lets the constraint decide, Clang and GCC find the conversion ambiguous.

p22.why: Defaulted parameters and the ellipsis take no part, so T* wins over T.

p23.why: Id<T>::type is non-deduced in one direction and matches only itself in the other, so f(T*, T*) is more specialized.

p24.why: Same pattern, so the constrained partial specialization is more specialized when it holds.

p25.why: A leading T beats a bare pack, and A&... beats A..., also for an empty tail.

p26.why: The lists differ in length counting defaults, so the constraint does not decide on Clang and GCC (ambiguous); EDG lets it decide.

p27.why: The two reference pairs prefer opposite templates.

p28.why: For an lvalue, T& wins over T&&.

p29.why: After stripping, both are T, and only one was a reference.

p30.why: pair(T, T) is more specialized than pair(T, U); with mixed types only the second is viable.

p31.why: The member gets an object parameter of the right reference kind, and T* beats U.

p32.why: The defaulted parameter takes no part, so the two templates tie.

p33.why: T* is a more specialized result than T.

p34.why: auto** orders before auto*, which orders before auto.

p35.why: The heads match, and Strong subsumes Weak.

p36.why: R takes part in no compared type, so it needs no value, and T* beats T.

p37.why: Both delete templates match the placement form, and T* is more specialized, so called is 1 and main returns 0.

p38.why: A qualified name through an invented type matches only itself, so f(T, T) and g(T, int) are more specialized.

p39.why: Each template is better in one position.

p40.why: U takes part in no compared type, so f(T*) is more specialized.

p41.why: Clang adds the object parameter before reversal and picks the member (true); GCC and EDG pick the non-member, so the assertion fails.
